name: SunVox Studio
description: AI-operable music engine — inspect, render and compose SunVox/XM/MOD tracker projects via the MIT-licensed SunVox library. Headless offline rendering (~130x realtime, no audio device) and programmatic composition from JSON specs (patterns, arrangement, song name). Renders and projects are saved to Crow storage; a render can go straight into a Funkwhale library for glasses playback.
author: Crow

env_vars.name: SUNVOX_WORKDIR
env_vars.description: Where rendered audio and composed projects are written.

env_vars.name: SUNVOX_READ_DIRS
env_vars.description: Extra folders (colon-separated) the tools may read project files from, besides the work dir. Name narrow music folders only; never /, .. or a home directory.

env_vars.name: SUNVOX_MAX_RENDER_SECONDS
env_vars.description: Longest render allowed, in seconds (default 1200, at most 3600).

notes: Vendors libsunvox 2.1.4d (MIT, (c) Alexander Zolotov / WarmPlace.ru) for linux x86_64 — see vendor/LICENSE.txt; the prebuilt library's terms ("Powered by SunVox" attribution) and the SunDog/libFLAC/Tremor licences are in vendor/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt. No Docker, no network ports: a pure stdio MCP server around the local engine library. Saves to Crow storage through the app's s3-client (MINIO_* env) and records storage_files rows; the Funkwhale upload uses the Funkwhale add-on's own configuration (the same one the gateway's media relay reads). Linux x86_64 only in v1 (arm64 .so available upstream).
